reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses HEA coatings and Mn dissolution in molten fluoride salts, respectively; neither provides any data or discussion on the native oxide scale of Q235 steel, its room-temperature passivation, or its high-temperature instability in sulfate/chloride salts. The key premises are therefore entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Q235 steel has a native iron oxide scale that is passivating at room temperature
At 700–900 °C, this oxide scale becomes unstable (dissolution, spallation, or phase transformation)
Oxide scale instability leads to loss of protection and accelerated metal loss
A stable reference system (e.g., stainless steel) retains protection at high temperature
